subject: Endpoint traffic simulation and SLA evidence
messages:
From: Alicia Monroe <alicia.monroe@novatech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@novatech.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 13:22:00 -0400
Subject: RFP follow-up: traffic simulation & SLA evidence request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP packet. Procurement reviewed the high-level materials and asked for a deeper set of artifacts focused on performance validation before we move to the legal and security checkpoints. Specifically we need: 

- A documented traffic simulation matrix (distribution of prompt lengths, concurrency mix, request types e.g., chat/generation/embeddings) that you used to produce published SLAs.
- Test harness code or a description of the harness (seeding, orchestration, how you mix burst/test phases).
- Raw or sampled request/response traces (anonymized) covering at least two 6-hour runs (steady-state + burst injection).
- Methodology for measuring tail latency (p99/p999), cold start accounting, and how caching/batching influenced results.
- Evidence of autoscaling/graceful degradation under capacity pressure (e.g., canary fallback metrics, replica spin-up times).
- Notes on model variants used during testing (quantized vs full precision), and any kernel/compilation flags that materially affect latency.

Can you provide these artifacts or point us to a drive bundle we can review? If there are any constraints (IP, redaction), please call them out. We're trying to complete this evidence review by next Friday (2027-10-08).

Cheers,
Alicia
Alicia Monroe
Sr. Procurement Manager — Novatech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Monroe <alicia.monroe@novatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 16:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: traffic simulation & SLA evidence request

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching a workbook that contains the traffic matrices, run manifests, and summary artifacts ("novatech_benchmark_workbook_v2.xlsx"). For quick highlights: 

- Topline steady-state: 20k tokens/sec sustained across a 4-replica cluster (NVLink) with 95th/99th latency targets of <= 120ms / <= 420ms for 512-token average prompts on our verified M-XXL config.
- Burst scenario: 3x surge for 10 minutes; autoscaler added up to 2 additional replicas within 90s and we saw tail rises to ~900ms on p99 during warm-up.
- Cold starts: measured cold-start 95th at 1.8s for a new replica under a standard image; we show mitigation via pre-warmed standby pools in Dedicated.
- Caching & batching: prefix/KV caching reduces token compute by ~22% on conversational workloads in our tests; continuous batching decreased avg per-token latency by ~12% under moderate QPS.

Attached items & where to find the raw traces: 
- novatech_benchmark_workbook_v2.xlsx (traffic matrices, run manifests, measurement scripts)
- request_log_samples_20270928.jsonl (anonymized sampled requests)
- response_traces_summary.tar.gz (aggregated traces + p99/p999 plots)

Notes on methodology (summary, full text in workbook): 
- Traffic synthesis: we seed a 3-hour steady-state using a mixture of 70% small prompts (<64 tokens), 25% mid (64-512), 5% long (>512). Bursts are injected by scaling the small-prompt generator to 3x planned QPS for 10/30/60s windows.
- Tail latency: p99/p999 measured at the per-route level using sliding windows (1m/5m buckets) with service-time decomposition for queueing vs. execution. We annotate whether traces include KV cache hits.
- Isolation: test runs on isolated VPCs with host-level telemetry (perf counters), and we provide process-level logs to confirm no noisy neighbor impact.

I'll also schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive to walk engineering through the workbook. Ben and Karthik are included on the call to cover runtime and kernel-level notes. Can you confirm availability for Thursday 2027-10-07 or Friday 2027-10-08?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 18:12:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: clarifications to include in Novatech packet

Marissa — quick internal note to append to the workbook before the deep-dive. Copy into the RFP bundle: 

1) Batching knobs: show the default continuous-batcher config (max_batch_tokens, max_duration_ms) and a sensitivity table showing latency/cost trade-offs at 250/500/1000 concurrent request levels.
2) KV cache: provide hit-rate curves for conversational profiles and indicate the policy for cache warm-up on new replicas (we use prefix prefetch for common session tokens).
3) Quantization/Compilers: include the model variant table — Q4_0 vs Q3_B — plus the kernel selection mapping file (kernel_map_v3.txt) that shows which optimized kernels were used per op (attention, matmul) on NVLink vs PCIe hosts.
4) Failure modes: add the graceful-degradation timeline (how and when we fallback to smaller model variant or region) and the threshold values that trigger fallback.

I added a short example snippet for the harness (how we seed unique session IDs to preserve cache realism) and a link to our orchestration runbook. Ping me if you want me to join the call and walk through the kernel map.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Alicia — legal/procurement quick question: for the raw traces you plan to provide, can you confirm the anonymization steps and whether the test VPCs contain any customer data? We need a short attestation for our audit folder addressing: 

- Data residency during tests (host regions, e.g., us-east-1)
- Anonymization: what fields are scrubbed from request/response samples and the hash/salting approach if you provide session identifiers
- Retention of test artifacts (how long Redwood keeps the raw traces)

If you have a standard attestation text we can include in our security appendix, please share.

Thanks,

Security & Procurement — DataBank Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Andre Silva <andre.silva@databancorp.com>, Alicia Monroe <alicia.monone@novatech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 11:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: traffic simulation & SLA evidence request

Andre — good questions. Short attestation below and full redaction checklist included in the workbook (tab: "PII_Redaction").

- Data residency: all test runs for Novatech were executed in our isolated test VPC in us-east-1 (AWS) with customer-facing endpoints disabled.
- Anonymization: request/response samples were sanitized to remove PII and payloads. Session ids in samples were replaced with salted hashes (SHA-256 with per-run salt). No raw customer payloads are included.
- Retention: raw traces are retained for 90 days by default and then moved to a locked archival bucket for 12 months for audit purposes; extracts provided to customers are retained per the contract.

If you need an explicit signed attestation, we can generate a short PDF signed by our security lead; otherwise the workbook's PII_Redaction tab plus the supplied sample files should be sufficient for procurement review.

Best,
Marissa
